messages.content: Can you provide the address for latitude 37.4224764 and longitude -122.0842499 using the Geocoding API?

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

message.content:
Sure! To get the human‑readable address for those coordinates you would normally hit a **reverse‑geocoding** endpoint such as:

| Service | Endpoint |
|---------|----------|
| **Google Maps Geocoding API** | `https://maps.googleapis.com/maps/api/geocode/json?latlng={LAT},{LNG}&key={API_KEY}` |
| **OpenStreetMap Nominatim** | `https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org/reverse?format=jsonv2&lat={LAT}&lon={LON}` |

Below is what you’d typically see when querying each one with your coordinates (`latitude = 37.4224764`, `longitude = –122.0842499`).  
*(Replace `{API_KEY}` with a valid key.)*

---

### 1️⃣ Google Maps Geocoding API

```http
GET https://maps.googleapis.com/maps/api/geocode/json?
   latlng=37.4224764,-122.0842499&
   key=YOUR_GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY
```

#### Sample Response (truncated)

```json
{
  "results": [
    {
      "address_components": [
        { "long_name": "1600",          "short_name": "1600",         "types": ["street_number"] },
        { "long_name": "Amphitheatre Pkwy", "short_name": "Amphitheatre Pkwy",
          "types": ["route"] },
        { "long_name": "Mountain View", "short_name": "Mountain View",
          "types": ["locality", "political"] },
        { "long_name": "Santa Clara County", "short_name": "Santa Clara County",
          "types": ["administrative_area_level_2", "political"] },
        { "long_name": "California", "short_name": "CA",
          "types": ["administrative_area_level_1", "political"] },
        { "long_name": "United States", "short_name": "US",
          "types": ["country", "political"] }
      ],
      "formatted_address": "1600 Amphitheatre Parkway, Mountain View, CA 94043, USA",
      "geometry": {...},
      "place_id": "...",
      "plus_code": {...}
    }
  ],
  "status": "OK"
}
```

> **Result:** `"1600 Amphitheatre Parkway, Mountain View, CA 94043, USA"`

---

### 2️⃣ OpenStreetMap Nominatim (free & public)

```http
GET https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org/reverse?
   format=jsonv2&
   lat=37.4224764&
   lon=-122.0842499
```

#### Sample Response (truncated)

```json
{
  "place_id": 123456789,
  "licence": "Data © OpenStreetMap contributors ...",
  "osm_type": "way",
  "osm_id": 987654321,
  "lat": "37.4224764",
  "lon": "-122.0842499",
  "display_name": "1600, Amphitheatre Parkway, Mountain View, Santa Clara County, California, 94043, United States",
  "address": {
    "house_number": "1600",
    "road": "Amphitheatre Parkway",
    "city": "Mountain View",
    "county": "Santa Clara County",
    "state": "California",
    "postcode": "94043",
    "country": "United States",
    "country_code": "us"
  },
  ...
}
```

> **Result:** `"1600, Amphitheatre Parkway, Mountain View, Santa Clara County, California, 94043, United States"`  

Both services will return essentially the same address – “1600 Amphitheatre Parkway, Mountain View, CA” – which is the well‑known Google headquarters.

---

### Quick Summary

* **Coordinates → Address**  
  *Latitude:* 37.4224764 Longitude:* −122.0842499  
  ➜ **Address:** `1600 Amphitheatre Parkway, Mountain View, CA 94043, USA`

Feel free to plug the coordinates into whichever reverse‑geo API you prefer. Let me know if you'd like help constructing the exact curl command or handling pagination / rate limits!
